mainTopic: The end of פרק כל הבשר (blood and its exclusions), and the new chapter on attached parts and שומרים for טומאת אוכלין versus טומאת נבלות
overview: This amud finishes one chapter and begins the next. First the גמרא explains that limiting words in the פסוקים of תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה keep their special rule of מעילה from spreading to other cases. Then it explains why three phrases are needed about the blood of קרבנות: each one frees blood from a different prohibition, namely נותר, מעילה, and eating קדשים while טמא. No phrase is needed for פיגול, because blood is itself the מתיר, and פיגול applies only to things that something else permits. Then פרק כל הבשר ends, and a new משנה opens. It teaches that parts attached to meat, like the hide and bones, join with the meat to reach a כביצה for טומאת אוכלין, but not a כזית for טומאת נבלות. The גמרא calls these parts שומרים. It finds the source that they count for light impurity in seeds sown in their shells. It finds the source that they do not count for severe impurity in the word ״בנבלתה״.

steps.title: Limiting words keep the rule inside these two cases
steps.stepSummary: The rule that מעילה still applies after the מצוה is done is not extended to other cases, because the פסוקים of תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה contain limiting words.
steps.simpleTranslation: Limiting words are written. Here (by תרומת הדשן) it says "and he shall put it," and there (by עגלה ערופה) it says "whose neck was broken."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering an earlier question: why don't we learn from these two cases that מעילה applies to other items after their מצוה is done? It answers that each פסוק has a limiting word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the rule is that once an item's מצוה is done, there is no more מעילה. תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה are exceptions. The word "וְשָׂמוֹ" ("it") and the extra description "הָעֲרוּפָה" show that the exception applies only to these two cases and to nothing else.

keyTerms.meaning: Exclusions: words in a פסוק that limit a law to a specific case
"And he shall put it": said about the ashes of תרומת הדשן
The calf whose neck is broken when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown
The prohibition against using or benefiting from הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying the rule of מעילה after a מצוה applies everywhere. The opposite is true: the limiting words teach that this exception stays inside these two cases only.

phrases.english: Exclusions are written:
phrases.notes: He means each of the two cases has a word that limits the law to that case alone.

phrases.english: here it is written: "And he shall put it,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:3, about the ashes of תרומת הדשן.

phrases.english: there it is written: "whose neck was broken."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to a question asked on the previous page, about why these two exceptions don't teach a general rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual limitation: the פסוקים themselves restrict the rule to their own cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think that two cases sharing the same rule could teach that rule for all other items too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Limiting words in each פסוק confine the rule of מעילה after the מצוה to תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה only.

steps.title: Why do we need three phrases about blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the blood of קרבנות and asks why three separate phrases are needed to exclude it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need three verses about blood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to an earlier topic, the three phrases teaching that the blood of קרבנות is excluded. It asks why one phrase would not have been enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, three phrases were used to teach that blood is not subject to מעילה. The question assumes the Torah does not repeat itself for no reason. So each phrase should be teaching something of its own.

keyTerms.meaning: Verses, or phrases from a פסוק
Why do I need it? This asks what each source adds
Blood, here meaning the blood of a קרבן

phrases.english: And why do I need three verses regarding blood?
phrases.notes: These are the three phrases from ויקרא 17:11 that were quoted earlier about the blood of קרבנות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה and returns to the earlier topic of blood.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each of the three phrases about blood comes to teach, so that none of them is extra.

steps.title: Each phrase excludes blood from a different prohibition
steps.stepSummary: One phrase excludes blood from נותר, one from מעילה, and one from eating קדשים while טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is to exclude blood from נותר, one is to exclude it from מעילה, and one is to exclude it from טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Each phrase teaches that blood is free from a different prohibition that normally applies to קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who eats the meat of a קרבן can be liable for נותר, for מעילה, or for eating it while טמא. Blood is different. The three phrases free it from all three of these extra prohibitions, so a person who consumes it violates only the prohibition of eating blood.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude: to teach that a law does not apply
Meat of a קרבן left over past its allowed time
Ritual impurity; here, eating קדשים while impure

steps.whatToRemember: Blood of a קרבן is excluded from three prohibitions by three phrases: נותר, מעילה, and טומאה.

phrases.english: One is to exclude it from notar,
and one is to exclude it from misuse of consecrated property,
and one is to exclude it from ritual impurity.
phrases.notes: He means the prohibition against eating קדשים while you are טמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three phrases exclude blood from נותר, מעילה, and טומאה.

steps.title: No verse is needed to exclude blood from פיגול
steps.stepSummary: A משנה already teaches that פיגול applies only to things that are permitted by something else. Blood is itself what permits the קרבן, so it is not subject to פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for פיגול no verse is needed, as we learned: anything that has permitting factors, whether for a person or for the מזבח, one is liable for it because of פיגול. And blood is itself the permitting factor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why there isn't a fourth phrase to exclude blood from פיגול. A משנה already shows that blood could never be פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says פיגול applies to things that become permitted through something else. The sprinkling of the blood is what permits the meat to people and the parts that go on the מזבח. Since blood is the thing that permits, not a thing that gets permitted, it falls outside פיגול without any special verse.

keyTerms.meaning: A קרבן made invalid by the intention to eat it after its allowed time; eating it brings כרת
Permitting factors: the act, like sprinkling the blood, that makes the קרבן allowed
The altar
No verse is needed, because the law is already known from another source

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why only three exclusions are needed and not four. It also teaches a general principle: the thing that permits a קרבן is not itself subject to פיגול.
steps.whatToRemember: פיגול applies only to things that have a מתיר. Blood is the מתיר itself, so it can't become פיגול.

phrases.english: But to exclude it from piggul no verse is needed,
as we learned: Anything that has permitting factors,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in זבחים 43a.

phrases.english: whether for a person or for the altar,
phrases.notes: Meaning whether it makes the meat allowed for people to eat or allowed to be burned on the מזבח.

phrases.english: one is liable for it due to piggul,
and blood itself is a permitting factor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מִפִּגּוּל לָא צְרִיךְ קְרָא, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to the answer of step 3 by explaining why פיגול is missing from the list of exclusions.
steps.raayaObject: That blood is not subject to פיגול even without a verse.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in זבחים: anything that has מתירין can become פיגול, and blood is itself the מתיר.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק כל הבשר
steps.stepSummary: The chapter כל הבשר comes to an end with the traditional closing line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter כל הבשר.
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes the chapter we have been learning, פרק כל הבשר. It is not part of the argument. It marks the end of one chapter before a new one starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion about blood, פיגול and the limiting words in the פסוקים is now finished. Whatever comes next starts a brand-new topic with its own משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you": the traditional line said when finishing a chapter
The name of the chapter being finished, taken from its opening words

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter "All Meat."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final proof about blood and פיגול.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק כל הבשר is complete. A new chapter begins.

steps.title: Attached parts join the meat for food impurity, not carcass impurity
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists parts attached to meat that join with it to reach the size needed for טומאת אוכלין, but not the size needed for טומאת נבלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The hide, the gravy, the spices, the meat residue, the bones, the tendons, the horns and the hooves all join together with the meat to make it big enough to give over food impurity. They do not join for carcass impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה. It lists parts that are stuck to meat and says they count together with the meat for טומאת אוכלין, but not for טומאת נבלות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure food passes on impurity only if it is כביצה (an egg's size). The משנה says that these attached parts help the meat reach that size even though they are not real meat. For טומאת נבלות, which needs a כזית (an olive's size), they do not help, so only the real meat counts there.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: the label that marks the start of a משנה
They join together (to complete a required size)
Food impurity: impurity that food passes on to other food and drink, needing a כביצה
Carcass impurity: the stronger impurity of a dead animal, needing a כזית
The size of an egg, the amount needed for טומאת אוכלין
The size of an olive, the amount needed for טומאת נבלות

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these parts can make food impure by themselves. They only help real meat reach the needed size, and only for food impurity.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets up the whole chapter's topic: the difference between the rules of טומאת אוכלין and טומאת נבלות.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The hide, and the gravy,
and the spices, and the meat residue,
phrases.notes: אלל means the bits of meat left stuck to the hide after skinning the animal.

phrases.english: and the bones, and the tendons,
and the horns, and the hooves —
join together to impart the impurity of food,
phrases.notes: They join with the meat to make up the egg-size needed for food impurity.

phrases.english: but not the impurity of animal carcasses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן. It does not depend on the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Parts attached to meat join with it to reach a כביצה for טומאת אוכלין, but do not join to reach a כזית for טומאת נבלות.

steps.title: A twitching slaughtered animal, and the general rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a similar case, a slaughtered non-kosher animal that is still twitching. It then sums up: the Torah included more things in טומאת אוכלין than in טומאת נבלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the same way, if someone slaughters a non-kosher animal for a non-Jew and it is still twitching, it gives over food impurity but not carcass impurity, until it dies or its head is cut off. So the Torah included more things in food impurity than in carcass impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second example of something that has טומאת אוכלין but not טומאת נבלות. Then it states the general idea behind both examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A twitching animal is not yet dead, so it is not a נבלה and cannot give over carcass impurity. It already counts as food, though, so it can give over food impurity. Once it dies or its head is cut off, it becomes a נבלה. The closing line explains both cases: food impurity covers a wider range of things than carcass impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: Similarly: introduces another case that follows the same pattern
A non-kosher animal
Twitching: still moving after being slaughtered
The Torah included (widened the category)

steps.whatToRemember: טומאת אוכלין is wider than טומאת נבלות. Attached parts and a still-twitching animal count for food impurity, but not for carcass impurity.

phrases.english: Similarly,
one who slaughters a non-kosher animal for a gentile
and it is still twitching,
it imparts the impurity of food,
but not the impurity of animal carcasses

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁתָּמוּת אוֹ עַד שֶׁיַּתִּיז אֶת רֹאשָׁהּ.
phrases.english: until it dies or until one cuts off its head.
The Torah included more to impart the impurity of food
than what it included to impart the impurity of animal carcasses.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ, הַשּׁוֹחֵט בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה לְגוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second example of the same pattern from step 6, then states the general rule behind both.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slaughtered, still-twitching non-kosher animal has טומאת אוכלין but not טומאת נבלות until it dies or is beheaded. The Torah included more in טומאת אוכלין than in טומאת נבלות.

steps.title: רבי יהודה on gathered scraps of meat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that scraps of meat stuck to the hide, if gathered into an olive's size in one place, carry full liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: scraps of meat stuck to the hide, if they are gathered together and there is an olive's size of them in one place, one is liable for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with רבי יהודה's opinion about אלל, the little bits of meat left on the hide after skinning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה listed אלל among the parts that join only for טומאת אוכלין. רבי יהודה adds a condition: if the scraps are gathered into one spot and reach a כזית, they count as real carcass meat. Then they bring full liability, not just the lighter food impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: Small scraps of meat that stay stuck to the hide after skinning
Gathered together in one place
An olive's size, the measure needed for טומאת נבלות
Liable, held responsible under the law

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends here: many attached parts join for טומאת אוכלין only, but רבי יהודה says a gathered כזית of אלל counts as real carcass meat.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The scraps of meat that are gathered together,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ כְּזַיִת בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד –
phrases.english: if there is an olive's size of it in one place,
one is liable for it.
phrases.notes: He means it is treated like real carcass meat, not just a part that joins with the meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a dissenting condition to the משנה's list of parts that join only for טומאת אוכלין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gathered אלל of a כזית in one place counts as carcass meat and brings liability.

steps.title: The משנה already teaches a known ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה contains the ברייתא's rule: protective parts count for light impurity but not for severe impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא. We have already learned in our משנה what רבנן taught: protective parts count for a light impurity, but protective parts do not count for a severe impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by pointing out that our משנה already teaches a rule that a ברייתא states outright. This sets up the questions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hide and similar parts in the משנה are called שומרים, parts that guard the food. They join for טומאת אוכלין, the light impurity, but not for טומאת נבלות, the severe impurity. The גמרא shows that our משנה matches the ברייתא's general rule, and then looks for the source of each half of that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Protective parts that guard the food, like a shell or hide
A light impurity, like טומאת אוכלין, which passes only to food and drink
A severe impurity, like טומאת נבלות, which passes to people and vessels

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two measures: טומאת אוכלין is measured by an egg's size (כביצה), and טומאת נבלות by an olive's size (כזית). The protective parts help reach only the first one.

phrases.english: GEMARA.
We have already learned that which the Rabbis taught:
protective parts count for a light impurity,
phrases.notes: Count here means the protective part joins with the food to reach the needed size.

phrases.english: but protective parts do not count for a severe impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by linking the משנה to a general rule stated in a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Protective parts join with food for light impurity, but not for severe impurity.

steps.title: Source for protective parts counting for light impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that protective parts join with food for a light impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that protective parts count for a light impurity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the first half of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shell or hide is not normal food, so it is surprising that it should join with food for any impurity. The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: From where do we know that protective parts count for a light impurity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first half of the rule from step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that protective parts join for טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: Seeds are sown in their shells
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל learns from ״על כל זרע זרוע״ that seeds count the way they are sown, with their shells.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: "Upon any sowing seed that is sown": in the way people take it out for sowing, wheat in its shell, barley in its shell, and lentils in their shells.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל on the פסוק about food impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of seed "that is sown," and people sow grain still in its shell. So the Torah treats the seed together with its shell as one unit for food impurity. This shows that a protective part joins with the food for the light impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: Seed that is sown
Shell or husk

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"Upon any sowing seed that is sown":
in the way that people take it out for sowing:
wheat in its shell,
and barley in its shell,
and lentils in their shells.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ״על כל זרע זרוע״ includes the seed in its shell, as it is sown, so protective parts join for light impurity.

steps.title: Source for protective parts not counting for severe impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that protective parts do not join for a severe impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that protective parts do not count for a severe impurity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the source of the second half of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since protective parts do join for the light impurity, one might think they also join for טומאת נבלות. The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows they do not.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that protective parts do not count for a severe impurity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question for the second half of the rule from step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that protective parts do not join for טומאת נבלות.

steps.title: "Its carcass" excludes hide without meat
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from ״בנבלתה״ that only the carcass itself makes one impure, not hide without a כזית of meat on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: "Its carcass": but not hide that does not have an olive's size of meat on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that reads the word ״בנבלתה״ narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says one who touches "its carcass" becomes impure, meaning the actual flesh. Hide that does not have a כזית of meat on it is not the carcass, so it does not bring טומאת נבלות. This shows that a protective part like hide does not join for the severe impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: "Its carcass," the dead animal's actual flesh
Hide or skin

steps.whatToRemember: Protective parts join with food for טומאת אוכלין, learned from seeds sown in their shells. They do not join for טומאת נבלות, learned from ״בנבלתה״, which excludes hide without a כזית of meat.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"Its carcass":

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בְּעוֹר שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר.
phrases.english: but not hide that does not have an olive's size of meat on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 with a ברייתא's reading of a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״בנבלתה״ limits טומאת נבלות to the flesh itself, excluding hide without a כזית of meat.
